translations.text: A discourse by Saint Epiphanius, Archbishop of Cyprus, on the burial of the body of our Lord Jesus Christ, on Joseph of Arimathea and Nicodemus, and on the descent of our Lord.

[?] burial [?], after the saving Passion had wondrously taken place. What is this great silence on earth today? What is this great silence and this great stillness? A great silence, because the King is sleeping. The earth grew afraid and fell silent, because God fell asleep in the flesh. God fell asleep in the flesh, and Hades trembled. God slept for a little while and raised from Hades those who had been sleeping from ages past. Where now are yesterday’s uproars, voices, and outcries raised against Christ by the lawbreakers?
Where are the crowds and the ranks, the weapons and the clubs? Where are the kings and the priests, and the judges who stand condemned?
Where are the torches and swords, and the countless outcries? Where are the peoples and their rage, and their unjust toil? Truly, indeed, exceedingly so.
Truly, the peoples pondered vain and senseless things. They stumbled against the cornerstone, Christ, and shattered themselves. They hurled themselves against the solid rock.
but their waves dissolved into foam. They struck against the invincible anvil, but were themselves crushed.

They lifted the stone onto the tree, and when he descended, he put them to death. They bound the great Samson, Christ the Sun, but he broke the everlasting bonds and destroyed the foreigners and the lawbreakers. God the Sun went down beneath the earth and brought the deepest darkness upon the Jews. Today there is salvation for those on earth and for those who have been beneath the earth from ages past. Today there is salvation for the whole world, all that we see and all that we do not see.

Today the Lord’s coming is twofold; his saving work is twofold; his love for humanity is twofold; his descent is twofold, together with his humiliation. His visitation to humanity is twofold: God comes from heaven to earth, and from the earth to beneath the earth. The gates of Hades are opening. You who have been sleeping from ages past, rejoice! You who sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, receive the great light! The Lord is with the slaves, God with the dead, Life with those who have died.

The innocent one is with the guilty; the unfading Light is with those in darkness; the Liberator is with the captives; he who is above the heavens is with those in the depths below. We believed in Christ on earth; Christ is among the dead—let us descend with him. Let us learn the mysteries that are there; let us understand God’s mystery, the hidden wonders beneath the earth. Let us learn how he has enlightened even those in Hades through his preaching. Does God, appearing in Hades, then save everyone without distinction? No, but there too he saves those who believe. Yesterday he performed the works of his saving plan, but today the works of the Master. Yesterday he performed the works of the flesh, but today the works of the Lord. Yesterday he revealed human things, but today divine things. Yesterday he was struck on the ear, but today, with the radiance of his divinity, he strikes the dwelling of Hades. Yesterday he was bound; today he binds the tyrant with bonds that cannot be loosened.
Yesterday he was being condemned; today he grants freedom to the condemned.

Yesterday Pilate’s servants mocked him; today the gatekeepers of Hades saw him and vanished. So listen to the lofty account of Christ’s suffering. Listen and sing praise. Listen and glorify him. Listen and proclaim God’s great wonders: how the law gives way, how grace blossoms, how the foreshadowings pass away, how the truth is proclaimed, how the shadow passes away, how the sun fills the inhabited world, how the old law has grown old, how the new law is announced, how the old things have passed away, how the new things have blossomed.
Two peoples came to Zion at the time of Christ's suffering: the Jews
And the Gentiles together as well: two rulers, Pilate and Herod; two priests, Annas and Caiaphas.
So that both Passovers might take place together, one ending and Christ’s beginning. Two sacrifices were being offered that evening, since salvation, I say, was coming to the living and the dead.
The Jews bound and slaughtered a lamb, while the Gentiles slaughtered God in the flesh.
Some looked toward the shadow, while others hastened toward the sun and toward God. Some bound Christ and sent him away, while those from among the Gentiles received him in a different spirit.
The Jews remembered the exodus from Egypt, while those from among the Gentiles proclaimed deliverance from deception.
And see where: in Zion, the city of the great King, in which he also brought about salvation in the midst
of the earth. Jesus, the Son of God, was made known between two living beings: between the Father and the Spirit,
For both lives, Life from Life, appearing as the true life; born in a manger between angels and human beings; lying as the cornerstone between the two peoples.
And proclaimed jointly by the law and the prophets, and between Moses and Elijah,
appearing on the mountain; and between the two robbers, appearing as God to the discerning robber; and between this present life and the life to come.
sitting as the eternal Judge; and today appearing between the living and the dead. Again, the power of life is twofold,

For the twofold birth and rebirth together [?]. And hear in these words the events of the twofold birth, and applaud the miracles. An angel announced his birth to Mary, Christ’s mother; an angel, to Mary Magdalene,
announced his rebirth from the tomb.
At night Christ is born in Bethlehem. A cave of stone is where Christ was born; a cave of stone is where Christ is born again. At his birth he receives swaddling clothes.
Here too he is wrapped in linen cloths. When he was born, he received myrrh; at his burial too he receives myrrh and aloes.
There was Joseph, Mary’s husband, who had not slept with her; here is Joseph of Arimathea. In Bethlehem the birth took place in a manger.
But the place in the tomb is also like that in the manger. The first
shepherds announce the good news of Christ’s birth.
And the first to announce to everyone the good news of Christ’s rebirth from the dead were also shepherds: Christ’s disciples.
There an angel cried out to the virgin, “Rejoice!” And here Christ, the angel of great counsel, cried out to the women, “Rejoice!”
At his first birth, after thirty days Christ entered the earthly Jerusalem, into the temple,

And as the firstborn he offered two young turtledoves to God. [?] at his burial from the dead [?]. After forty days Christ ascended into the Jerusalem above, from which he had never departed, into the true Holy of Holies,
as the incorruptible firstborn from the dead, offering to God the Father two young turtledoves: our soul and flesh.
God, the Ancient of Days, received him like another Simeon, as though into his hands, into his own bosom.
But if you hear these things in a worldly way rather than with faith, the unbroken seals refute you
of the Lord’s burial, of Christ’s tomb. For just as, while the enclosure of virginity was sealed and shut,

Christ was born of a virgin. In the same way, while the seals of the tomb remained unopened, Christ's birth took place. But how Christ, the Life, was once laid in the tomb, and by whom, let us hear from the holy words.
“When evening had come,” it says, “a rich man named Joseph came.” He boldly went in to Pilate
and asked for the body of Jesus. A man went in to a man, asking to receive the God
of mankind. Clay was asking clay to receive the Creator of all;
grass was asking grass to receive the fire of Gehenna; a little drop was asking a drop to receive the abyss.
Who has seen or who has ever heard of a man giving another man the Creator of mankind?

The lawless man promises to hand over the righteous one, the maker of laws. The condemned judge gives the Judge, as one condemned, to judges for burial. When evening had come, a man named Joseph arrived, truly rich because he received the whole body of the Lord. Truly rich because he received Christ's twofold nature from Pilate; rich because he was considered worthy to receive the priceless pearl. Truly rich, for he carried a treasury full of divine wealth. For how could he not be rich, having acquired the saving life of the whole world?
How could Joseph not be rich, having received as a gift the one who nourishes everyone and rules over all? When evening had come—
For the Sun of Righteousness had descended into Hades.
Therefore a rich man named Joseph came from Arimathea, who had kept himself hidden for fear of the Jews.
Nicodemus also came,
the man who had come to Jesus by night. Mysteries hidden within mysteries: two secret disciples go to hide Jesus in the tomb.
The hidden [?] in Hades, teaching the God hidden in the flesh through their own resurrection. Each outdoes the other in love for God: for Nicodemus, with myrrh
and aloes, is generous,
while Joseph is praiseworthy for his boldness toward Pilate.
For he cast aside every fear and boldly went in to Pilate, asking for the body of Jesus.
He went in and began with the greatest wisdom, so that he would not fail in his cherished intention. Therefore he does not begin with any grand speeches to Pilate,
lest he anger him and fail in his request. Nor does he say to him, “Give me the body of Jesus, who darkened the sun a short while ago,
and shattered the rocks, shook the earth, opened the tombs, and tore the curtain of the temple.” He says nothing of this kind to Pilate.
But what does he say? I have come to you, O judge, with a small request, asking for something very small.
Give me for burial the dead body of that man condemned by you: Jesus the Nazarene, Jesus the poor man,
Jesus the homeless one, this Jesus seen naked, the humble Jesus, Jesus the prisoner, the bloodied stranger, unknown among strangers and seen to be neglected by everyone.
“Give me this stranger. For what benefit do you gain from the body of this stranger?
Give me this Nazarene stranger, whose homeland we strangers do not know.
Give me this stranger, whose father we strangers do not know.
Give me this stranger, whose place and dwelling we strangers do not know.
Give me this stranger,
who has nowhere here to lay his head.
Give me this stranger among strangers,
a homeless stranger who, as a stranger, fled from Herod from the manger. Give me this stranger, who fled to Egypt while still in his swaddling clothes,
who has neither city nor village, neither house nor dwelling nor family in a foreign land, who has his dwelling with death and holds all things.

Give me, O master, this man hanging naked on the tree [?], so that I may cover him who covered the nakedness of my body. Give me this man who is dead and at the same time God, so that I may cover him who covered my sins,
Give me this dead man so that I may bury him who buried my sins in the Jordan.
I plead for a dead man who suffered wrong from everyone, who was betrayed by a friend,

betrayed by a disciple, driven out by his brothers, struck on the ear by his own slaves. I plead for the dead man, condemned by those he freed, given vinegar to drink for food, wounded by those he healed,
abandoned by his disciples, deprived of his own mother.
I beg you, Pilate, for the dead man hanging on the tree.
For he has no father on earth, nor any friend now, nor disciple, nor relative, nor anyone to bury him. He alone is the only-begotten Son of the One, God throughout the whole world, and no one else.
When Joseph had said these things to Pilate, Pilate ordered that the most holy body of Jesus be given to him.
He came to the place of Golgotha, took God in the flesh down from the tree, and laid
On earth, God in the flesh is naked, yet again not naked. And they see him lying below who raised all things on high; and he who is life and breath for all is briefly without breath.
And they see him without eyes who created the many-eyed beings. The resurrection of all lies on his back, and God, who raises the dead, is put to death in the flesh.
And the thunder of the word of God is silent in the flesh, and he who holds the earth in his hand is lifted by human hands. Then, Joseph, ask for him and receive him.
Do you know whom you received when you approached the cross and took Jesus down? Do you know whom you carried? If you know whom you hold, you have now become rich.
How, then, do you prepare a burial for this divine and awe-inspiring body? Your love is indeed praiseworthy.
But still more praiseworthy is the boldness of your soul. Do you not tremble, then, carrying in your arms him before whom the cherubim tremble?

With what fear will you strip the cloths from that divine flesh? With what reverence [?] to gaze trembling at his eyes and uncover the body of God, who humbled himself willingly? Tell me, then, Joseph: do you bury Jesus facing east as though he were dead, him who is the East of easts? And do you close Jesus’ eyes with your own fingers as though he were dead, when he opened the blind man’s eyes with his own finger? And do you press shut the lips of him who opened the mute man’s mouth?
And do you fold the hands of him who stretched out the withered hands? Or do you bind his feet according to the custom for the dead,
when he gave the power to walk to feet that could not move?
And do you lift onto a bier him who said to the man whose limbs were paralyzed, ‘Take up your bed and walk’?
And do you pour ointment upon the King, who is himself the ointment poured out that healed the whole world?
Come, then, while blood is still flowing from the wound in God's body, do you dare to squeeze it out of him, God who healed the woman with the flow of blood?
Come, then, do you wash with water the body of God, who washed everyone and granted cleansing?
What candles will you light for the true light, who has enlightened every human being?
What burial songs will you sing for him who continually receives songs from the heavenly powers? Do you shed tears, then, as over a dead man,
for him who wept and raised the dead Lazarus? Why, then, do you mourn
over him who gave joy to all and took sorrow away from Eve? Yet I call your hands blessed, Joseph, for they served and touched the still-bleeding divine body, Jesus’ hands and feet.
I call your hands blessed, for they touched God’s side

before unbelieving Thomas—faithful and praiseworthy [?]. I call your lips blessed, for they were filled without ever having enough, and pressed against Jesus’ lips, and were filled from there with the Holy Spirit. I call your eyes blessed, for they drew close to Jesus’ eyes.
and received the true light from there. I bless your face,
which pressed itself to God’s face. I bless your shoulders, which carried him who sustains humanity.
I bless your head, which Jesus, the head of all, touched. I bless Joseph and Nicodemus.
For you two became more cherubic than the cherubim, bearing God upon yourselves. Before the six-winged beings, you became God’s servants, covering God not with wings but with a shroud.
And you honored him before whom the cherubim tremble. You, Joseph and Nicodemus, carry him on your shoulders, while all the ranks of the bodiless beings carry him with them.
Where Joseph and Nicodemus are, have not all the hosts of God’s angels gathered there too?
The cherubim go ahead, the seraphim run before them, and the Thrones carry him with them.

And the six-winged ones cover themselves, and the many-eyed ones tremble, seeing Jesus in the flesh without eyes. And the powers veil themselves, and the dominions sing, and the ranks tremble. They marvel and are filled with dread, debating among themselves and saying, “What is this fearful word, this fear and trembling and dread? What is this great and astonishing wonder?”
God, who above is invisible to us bodiless beings, is seen below as a man, dead and naked.
Joseph and Nicodemus bury without hesitation him before whom the cherubim stand in reverence.”
When did he descend without abandoning those on high? How did he descend while remaining within? How did he come to earth, filling a human being? How did he come down without anyone noticing?
Being always on high with the Father as God, he had never appeared to us anywhere.
To human beings as a human being.
And at the same time he appeared as the lover of humankind. How does the invisible one become visible?
How did the bodiless one take flesh? How did the one beyond suffering accept suffering? How did the Judge stand before a tribunal? How did Life taste death?

How is the uncontainable one, being contained, confined in a tomb? How does he dwell in a tomb without leaving his Father’s throne? How does he enter the gates of a cave without opening the gates of heaven, yet opening the gates of paradise? He did not open the gates of virginity, but shattered the gates of Hades, and did not open the doors when Thomas was there.
But he opened the gates of the kingdom to humankind, while keeping the gates of the tomb and its seals intact.
How is he numbered among the dead, free even among the dead?
How does the light that never darkens come into the dark places and the shadows of death?

Where is he going? Where is he descending, he whom death cannot hold? What is the reason? What is the plan? What is the purpose of his descent into Hades? Perhaps he is descending to bring up Adam, the prisoner and our fellow servant.
Indeed, he is going to seek the first-created one, the lost sheep, and he wishes to visit those who sit in darkness and in the shadow of death.

For he is coming as God and as their son to free the captive Adam and the captive Eve from their sufferings. But let us descend with him. Let us join in the dance with him. Let us leap for joy. Let us
hasten. Let us accompany him. Let us sing praises. Let us stir ourselves, seeing God’s acts of reconciliation toward humankind and the release of the prisoners, which come from the good Lord.
For the true lover of humankind is coming, with courage and great authority, to lead out the prisoners held for ages, those who dwell in the tombs.
These were tormented by the unjust and unconquerable tyrant, who was tormented by God, having, as an adversary, stolen and gathered those who lived above.
There Adam is bound, the one who was bound before and died before all others, bound in the lowest depths. There is Abel, the first to be slaughtered and the first righteous man,

Christ’s shepherd, who became an image of the Shepherd in his unjust slaughter. There is Noah, an image of Christ, the builder of the great ark, God’s Church, who saved all the hard-hearted nations from the flood of ungodliness through the dove of the Holy Spirit, and drove the dark raven, the devil, out of it. There is Abraham, Christ’s forefather, the priest who offered God a godless and immortal sacrifice. There is Isaac in bonds, who long ago was bound by Abraham as an image of Christ. There is Jacob, sorrowful below in Hades, who long ago grieved for Joseph above.
There was Joseph, who had been bound in prison in Egypt, as a type of Christ, of the Lord’s imprisonment.
There is Moses below in the dark places, just as he was in the basket, below in the dark places. There is Daniel in the lowest tomb of Hades. There is Jeremiah, as though in a pit
of mud, in the tomb of Hades and in death’s decay. There Jonah lies in the belly of Hades.
In figures of Christ, eternal and before all ages. Jonah [?], to him who lives forever and ever, and for ages and beyond.
There was David, the forefather of God, from whom Christ was born according to the flesh. And why do I speak of David and Jonah and Solomon?
There is John himself, the great one and greater than all the prophets, proclaiming Christ to all those in the tombs as in the dark womb—a twofold forerunner.
and herald to the living and the dead, sent from Herod’s prison

Into the prison of souls, to the righteous and unrighteous who had died from the beginning of time. All the prophets and the righteous, with unceasing prayers, implored God from there, asking for deliverance from that grievous, pitiable dominion of the enemy and from the gloom of deepest darkness. And one of them said to God:
“From the belly of Hades [?] he heard my cry, my voice. He cast me into the depths. I cried out to you, O Lord. O Lord, hear my voice.”
And another: “Make your face shine, and we shall be saved.”
And another: “You who sit upon the cherubim, reveal yourself. Stir up your strength and come to save us.” And another: “Let your mercies hasten to meet us, O Lord.”
And another: “Deliver my soul from the lowest Hades.” And another: “O Lord, you have brought my soul up from Hades.”
And another: “Do not abandon my soul in Hades.” And another: “Let my life rise from corruption
“My [?] to you, O Lord my God.” See: to proclaim his love for humanity not only to those who died in his time and after him, but also to those held captive by Hades
before his coming, and to those sitting in darkness and in the shadow of death.

Therefore God the Word visited human beings who were in the flesh with flesh endowed with a soul. But the souls that were without flesh he enlightened in Hades with his own divine and most pure soul, which was separated from his body but not from his divinity.
Therefore let us make haste and go down in thought into Hades, so that we may see how there, at that time, with mighty power, he utterly restrains
the tyranny of the one who held sway, and the warriors [?]. With his radiance that does not die [?], he binds the ranks of the armies without hands [?], taking the gates of the abyss out of the way,
And Christ shattered the gates, which were not made of wood, with the cross, and crushed the nails and the everlasting bars.
and breaking them [?] with bonds, and with his own hands melting like wax the iron bonds that could not be loosened for him. And with the spear that pierced the divine side,
he pierced the tyrant’s incorporeal heart. There he shattered the strength of his bows, when with his divine hands he bent the cross like a bow, using the bonds as a bowstring.
Therefore, if you follow Christ in silence, you now see when he bound the tyrant,
where he impaled his head, how he demolished his prisons, how he led out the prisoners, how he ripped open the serpent, and where
he hung the serpent; how he freed Adam, how he raised Eve, and how he tore down the dividing wall;
and where he condemned the fierce serpent, how he established his invincible victories, where he put death to death,

And how he destroyed corruption and restored humanity to its original sovereign rank. Yesterday he rejected the sovereign legion of angels, saying to Peter, “I can now set before me more than twelve legions of angels.”

But today, in a manner worthy of God, and at the same time bravely and as sovereign, he descends upon Hades and upon death and upon the tyrant, through death—immortal death [?]. He has incorporeal warriors and invisible ranks [?], not merely legions, but tens of thousands upon tens of thousands and thousands upon thousands of angels and archangels,
authorities, principalities, dominions, powers, and thrones, the six-winged and many-eyed beings
of heavenly ranks escorting him as their own Lord and King,
bringing a gift and singing praises to Christ—not providing help in battle, for that is not fitting for God. What help does Christ need? Rather, they do this out of duty and honor,
with love for their own Lord, having been granted, like bodyguards, to stand continually before God.

So too the spearmen, swift in the Lord’s warfare, moved at a mere nod with divine swiftness, outstripping one another together, bringing things to completion in action, carrying out his commands, and with victory
arrayed, armed against enemies and tormentors.

Therefore they descended then, running together and following God and the Lord into the places of burial and the deepest places of all the earth, into the dwellings beneath the earth of those who had been dead from ages past, to bring out the chained prisoners who had slept from ages past. And when God’s visitation and his radiant coming reached the gates and the sunless dwellings of Hades, its dwellings and prisons, its hidden chambers and caverns, Gabriel, the commander-in-chief, went ahead of them all, bringing people joyful good news, as was his custom. With a mighty utterance, archangelic, radiant like a commander’s, and lionlike toward the hostile powers, he said in a loud voice, ‘Lift up your gates, you rulers!’
With them Michael cries, “And be lifted up, you everlasting gates!” Then the powers also said,
‘Stand aside, lawless gatekeepers! Likewise, you dominions with authority! Break apart, unbreakable iron bonds!’ And another: ‘Be put to shame, hostile adversaries!’ And another:
‘Be afraid, lawless tormentors!’ And behold, beside the valiant King, as they arm themselves royally and conquer, there is a kind of terror and trembling.
together with confusion and dreadful fear, falls upon the gates of the invincible ruler.
Likewise, at that wondrous coming of Christ into Hades, into the lowest regions, suddenly from above there came
Darkness before the flashing light [?], in the face of the hostile powers of Hades, as they hear a thunderous voice, with shouting and armies commanding and saying:
‘Lift up your gates, you rulers! Lift up the gates! Do not merely open them, but lift them up from their very foundations! Uproot them! Remove them!’

So that they may never be shut again. ‘Lift up your gates, you rulers!’ Not because the Master who has come is unable to enter when he commands, even with the gates shut, but because, as Master, he commands you, like wretched slaves, that the everlasting gates be lifted up, removed, and shattered.

Therefore he gives the command not to your multitudes, but to those who imagine themselves to be rulers, saying, ‘Lift up your gates, you rulers!’ Yet you are not rulers over anyone else. For even if until now you have wickedly ruled over those who have been dead from ages past, you shall no longer rule over them.
But neither over others nor over you.
Nor will you be rulers even over yourselves.
‘Lift up the gates! For Christ, the gate of heaven, has come. Make a way for him who has entered the westernmost west; the Lord is his name.’
And to the Lord belong the ways out through the gates of death.

You made the entrances of death, but he himself has come to make an exit. Therefore, ‘Lift up your gates, you rulers! Lift them up and do not delay! Lift them up quickly! Lift them up and do not wait!’ But if you intend to delay,
he commands the gates themselves to rise of their own accord, without hands: ‘Be lifted up, you gates
everlasting!’ At once the powers shouted; at once the gates were lifted up; at once the iron bonds and bars were shattered; at once the locks fell away.

At once the foundations of the prison were shaken. At once the hostile powers took to flight, pushing one another and stumbling over one another, each telling the other to flee. They were frightened and shaken; they were terrified and thrown into confusion; they turned pale and stood together.
They were astonished; together they were bewildered and trembled.
And one of them stood gaping, while another covered his face with his knees.
Another lay face down, gasping for breath. Another grew stiff as though dead. Another was gripped by terror and lay pale. Another was tormented in the innermost refuges.
For there Christ then struck off the heads of the mighty amid terror. There [?] trembled within him. There they loosened their tongues, saying:
“Who is this King of glory? Who is this, who performs such great wonders here among so many?
Who is this King of glory, who now does in Hades what has never happened in Hades before?”
“Who is this who leads out of here those who have been chained from ages past? Who is this who has destroyed our invincible dominion and strength?”
The Lord’s powers answered them, saying, “Do you wish to know who this King of glory is?
The Lord, strong and mighty; the Lord, mighty and strong and invincible in battle. He is the one who cast off—
you out of the heavenly places and sent you to the earth. O wretched, lawless tormentors!
He is the very one who crushed the heads of your serpents in the waters of the Jordan.
He is the very one who exposed you through the cross, made a spectacle of you, and weakened your sinews. He is the very one who bound you and plunged you into darkness
and sent you into the abyss. He is the very one who sends you into eternal fire and into Gehenna. Therefore do not delay.
Do not wait, but get moving and bring out the prisoners whom you have devoured until now. For your dominion has already been destroyed; your tyranny has already ceased.
Your fierce turmoil has been utterly destroyed. Your pride has been completely weakened. Your might has failed and perished.”
The Lord’s powers said these things to the hostile powers, and at the same time they hurried into action.
Some tore down the prisons from their very foundations, while others pursued the hostile powers,
who fled from the outer chambers into the inner ones. Others searched the deepest vaults, hiding places, and caves, running about.
Some brought one another bound to the Lord from elsewhere, while others bound the tyrant.

Others released those who had been bound for ages, and others swiftly attended to their duties. Some ran ahead of Christ as he entered within, while others stood before him as before God, King, and Victor. While these things were happening in this way,
and even greater things than these were taking place in Hades, and everyone was speaking
and everything was trembling at the Lord’s coming, the underworld itself was about to descend into still lower depths. That Adam—
that Adam, who had been bound before all other people,
held firmly bound in the innermost place of all, heard the Lord’s feet approaching the prisoners
and recognized the sound of his walking in the prison.
He turned to all those who had been prisoners with him from ages past and said, “I hear the sound of someone’s feet coming toward us. And if he has truly chosen to come here,
we shall be freed from our bonds. If we truly see him among us, we shall be delivered from our bonds.” While Adam was saying these and similar things to all those imprisoned with him,
the Lord came in to them, holding the victorious weapon of the cross.
When Adam, the first-created, saw him, he beat his breast in awe and cried out to all who had slept from ages past, saying, “My Lord be with all!”
Christ answered Adam, saying, “And with your spirit.” Taking him by the hand, he raised him up, saying:
“Awake, sleeper, and rise from the dead, and Christ will give you light.
I am your God, who for your sake became your son. Now I speak and with authority command the prisoners,
“Come out!” And to those in darkness, “Be enlightened!” And to those lying down, “Arise!” “I command you: awake, sleeper! For I did not create you to be held bound in Hades.”
Rise from the dead, for I am the life of humanity. Rise, my creation. Rise, my likeness, made in my image.
Get up; let us go from here. For you are in me and I am in you; we are one undivided body. For your sake, I, your God, became your son. For your sake, though I am Lord, I took on the form
of you, a slave. For your sake I, who am above the heavens, came to earth and beneath the earth.

of a human being for your sake. I became like a man without help, free even among the dead. For your sake, who went out of the garden, I was handed over to the Jews from a garden, and in a garden I was condemned.
See the spitting on my face, which I endured for your sake, to restore you to your first breath. See the blows on my cheeks, which I endured.
to restore your disfigured likeness to its original image. See the wounds on my shoulders, which I endured
to cast off the burden of your sins that lies upon your shoulders. See my hands nailed fast.
I who stretched out my hands on the tree for good, for your sake, who stretched out your hands toward the tree for evil.
See my feet, nailed and fastened to the tree, for the sake of your feet, which ran wickedly toward the tree on the sixth day.
Your condemnation took place on the sixth day, and I brought about your judgment and the opening of paradise.
I tasted gall for your sake, to heal you of the bitter pleasure of that sweet food.
I tasted vinegar to destroy the sour and bitter cup of your death, and I accepted a sponge.
To wash away the written record of your sin, I also accepted a reed, to write freedom for the human race. I fell asleep on the cross.
And I was pierced in the side with a spear for your sake, who fell asleep in paradise and brought forth Eve from your side.
My side has healed the pain of your side. My sleep will bring you out of the sleep of death. My spear has stopped the spear that turns against you. Therefore, get up.
Let us go from here. I led you out of the land of paradise. I am now establishing you in paradise, but on a heavenly throne.
I denied you the tree that was an image of life, but now I, who am wholly life, have shared myself with you.
I commanded the cherubim to guard you like a slave. I will make the cherubim bow down to you. You hid from God because you were naked.

But now you have hidden the naked God within yourself. You clothed yourself in a shameful garment of skin, but I, God, clothed myself in the garment of skin that is your flesh. Therefore, rise; let us go from here, from decay to incorruptibility, from death to life. Rise; let us go from here.
from darkness into eternal light. Arise and go from here, from suffering to joy.
Arise and go from here, from slavery to freedom, from prison to the Jerusalem above,
from chains to God, from pain to the food of paradise, from earth to heaven.
For this is why I died and rose again: to rule over both the living and the dead.
Therefore arise and go, for the heavenly Father awaits the lost sheep.
The ninety-nine angelic sheep await their fellow servant Adam:

When will he rise, when will he ascend and return to God? The throne of the cherubim has been prepared. Those who carry him up are swift. Alternatively: ready. The table has been prepared; the food is ready; the eternal shelters and dwellings.
The treasures of good things have been opened. The kingdom of heaven was prepared before the ages—things that no eye has seen and no ear has heard,
good things that have not entered the human heart await man. These and similar
As the Lord says these things, Adam, who is in him, rises together with him. And he raises with him [?], but also many bodies

of the saints who had died throughout the ages rose, proclaiming the Lord’s resurrection on the third day. Let us receive it joyfully, see it and embrace it, rejoicing with the angels, celebrating with the archangels, and together glorifying Christ, who has raised us from decay. To him be glory and dominion, with the Father who has no beginning and the most holy and life-giving Spirit, now and always and forever and ever. Amen.
